detail:
Key (NEW, UNSURE settled REAL): R7|fnn-csp-worker-loop|swallow:serious-condition:fault @ host/native/catchup-spool.lisp:59.

The worker catches any serious-condition and stores status :error, actual 0; the consumer (pull-service.lisp:597-601) reads only its truthiness, so the condition is never logged, classified or fenced. An OS error becoming a per-peer :error is by design (ACL2 decides the round's end), but a non-OS fnn-fault from the leaves (a bad write progress in fnn-write-progress) is downgraded to a peer I/O error without reaching the fence. The unknown-operation branch (:42) is unreachable because submit bounds the operation; the write case needs a kernel contract violation, hence low severity.
fix: Have the worker keep a non-fnn-os-error condition separately and make fnn-csp-worker-take / the consumer re-signal it as fnn-fault so it reaches the fence; keep fnn-os-error reduced to status.
notes: 10-06 20:13 Code fixed on lane/lock-host-fix-1 (take re-signals non-OS condition as fnn-fault; red/green via native_catchup_spool_source). R7 swallow key REMAINS: checker cannot see the cross-thread re-signal; needs failure_scopes row fnn-csp-worker-loop scope=result (like fnn-extent-executor-job), a contract edit outside this lane. Pending convergence natives (catchup/pull image natives).
title: fnn-csp-worker-loop reduces every serious-condition, including a non-OS fault, to status :error with no fence (R7)
